intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine talk again in Abu Dhabi
items.text: Russia and Ukraine held their first talks mediated by the United States in nine months on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi. The meeting lasted about four hours, and both sides agreed to carry on on Wednesday. Topics included prisoner exchanges and security guarantees for Ukraine. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the talks productive, while President Zelenskyy described them as constructive. However, the two countries remain divided over territory and the order of any steps to end the war.

gloss.mediate: to help two sides reach an agreement
gloss.security guarantee: a promise to protect a country from attack
gloss.prisoner exchange: an agreement where each side frees prisoners

items.title: Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts its newsroom
items.text: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's best-known independent newspapers, closed its Moscow newsroom on Monday. Authorities had named it a foreign agent, its landlord refused to renew the lease, and banks stopped handling donations from readers. The paper was founded in 1993 and had already lost its media licence. Its editor Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021. The Kremlin spokesman said the closure was normal change in the media industry, but journalists disagreed.

gloss.foreign agent: a legal label in Russia that adds strict rules for a person or group
gloss.lease: a contract to rent a building
gloss.renew: to extend an agreement for more time
gloss.donation: money given to support a cause

items.title: US Army officer arrested in Gloucestershire
items.text: British police arrested a 41-year-old US Army officer near Gloucester on Tuesday under the National Security Act. The investigation involved MI5, the FBI and US military counterintelligence. The man worked at NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks. Officials say he tried to obtain information that could be useful to Moscow, but no classified material was passed to Russia. Police are searching two places in Gloucestershire, and the suspect remains in custody.

gloss.counterintelligence: work to stop spying by other countries
gloss.search: to look carefully in a place for evidence

items.title: Tuchel names England squad for Croatia and Spain
items.text: Thomas Tuchel has named his England squad for the final two Nations League group games, at home to Croatia and away to Spain. England have nine points from three games and need one draw to reach the quarter-finals. Cole Palmer is not in the squad, while Josh King of Fulham and Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund have been called up. Ben White returns for the first time since March. Harry Kane could break Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps.

gloss.call up: to choose a player for a national team
gloss.cap: an appearance for a national team
gloss.quarter-final: a match with eight teams left in a competition
gloss.squad: the group of players chosen for a team
gloss.break a record: to do better than the best result so far

items.title: Sinner to miss the ATP Finals in Turin
items.text: Defending champion Jannik Sinner will miss the ATP Finals because of a knee injury. He told a press conference in Milan on Tuesday that he hopes to return for the Australian Open in 2027. World number one Alexander Zverev leads the eight-man field in Turin, and four players are first-time qualifiers. The round-robin stage starts on Sunday and the final is on 22 November. Carlos Alcaraz reached the event after beating Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final.

gloss.defending champion: the winner of the last tournament
gloss.qualifier: a player who has earned a place in an event
gloss.round-robin: a format where every player meets the others in a group
gloss.miss: to not take part in something

items.title: AI behind nearly a fifth of UK growth, says Bank
items.text: The Bank of England says artificial intelligence accounts for just under a fifth of UK economic growth since the start of 2026. The figure comes from the Bank's own estimate, not from official statistics. Firms say AI has raised their productivity by about 0.5% over three years. The Bank says the effect on jobs is close to zero for now, although AI is reducing hiring at some companies. It adds that the rise mainly reflects higher demand for AI products, such as memory chips.

gloss.account for: to make up a part of a total
gloss.productivity: how much work is done in a given time
gloss.memory chip: a small part inside computers that stores data

items.title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs linked to higher heart risk
items.text: A study in The Lancet Regional Health Europe has found that people with diabetes who stop taking GLP-1 drugs face double the risk of a heart attack, stroke or death. About four in 100 people who stopped had one of these events in a year, compared with two in 100 among those who continued. Researchers studied more than 80,000 people with type 2 diabetes in Italy. The study is observational, so it cannot prove that stopping causes the extra risk.

gloss.stroke: a serious medical event when blood stops reaching part of the brain
gloss.observational study: research that watches people without changing their treatment
gloss.type 2 diabetes: a long-term condition affecting blood sugar
gloss.risk: the chance of something bad happening

items.title: Bank of England raises rates to 4%
items.text: The Bank of England raised its main interest rate by 0.25 points to 4% last week. Members of the Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1, and one member wanted a bigger rise of 0.5 points. Inflation was 3.5% in September, and the Bank expects it to average 4.9% in the second quarter of 2027. Unemployment was 4.7% in the three months to August. The Bank also expects the economy to grow by 0.7% in the third quarter.

gloss.interest rate: the cost of borrowing money, shown as a percentage
gloss.inflation: the rate at which prices rise
gloss.unemployment: the number of people without a job who want one

items.title: GTA VI becomes most pre-ordered game on PlayStation
items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most pre-ordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store, according to PlayStation. Xbox says it is the most pre-ordered title ever on the Microsoft Store. The game launches on Thursday 19 November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Players could start preloading it on Tuesday, nine days early. The boxed version contains only a download code, not a disc. Its predecessor, GTA V, has sold nearly 235 million copies since 2013.

gloss.pre-order: to pay for a game before it is released
gloss.preload: to download a game before it can be played
gloss.launch: to release a product to the public
gloss.copy: one sold unit of a game or book

items.title: GTA VI will run at 30 frames per second on consoles
items.text: Rockstar Games says Grand Theft Auto VI is targeting 30 frames per second on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox. PS5 Pro owners will get improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution. Ray-traced shadows will be available only on the PS5 Pro. All PS5 players can use DualSense haptics, Tempest 3D Audio and faster load times. Rockstar also highlighted Xbox Cloud Gaming, and Remote Play will work on both PlayStation and Xbox.

gloss.frame rate: how many images a game shows each second
gloss.target: to aim to reach a goal
gloss.ray-traced: using a method that simulates how light behaves
